units.issue: Recovery of possession based on tenant subletting, assignment, or other parting with possession without written landlord consent
units.act: Delhi Rent Control Act, section 14(1), clause (b)
units.date_scope: The prohibited transfer conduct must occur on or after 9 June 1952
units.procedure_scope: Recovery order by the Controller on an application made in the prescribed manner; the supplied text concerns only the section 14(1) opening, proviso, and clause (b)

conditions.text: A court or Controller generally may not order recovery of possession in favour of a landlord against a tenant except on the statutory proviso grounds
conditions.quote: no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made by any court or Controller in favour of the landlord against a tenant

conditions.text: The Controller may make a recovery order only on an application made in the prescribed manner and on one or more specified grounds
conditions.quote: the Controller may, on an application made to him in the prescribed manner, make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on one or more of the following grounds only

conditions.text: The relevant conduct must occur on or after 9 June 1952
conditions.quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952

conditions.text: The tenant must have sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of all or part of the premises
conditions.quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises

conditions.text: The relevant conduct must have occurred without the landlord's written consent
conditions.quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord

limitations: Only the displayed section 14(1) opening, proviso, and complete clause (b) are supplied; other eviction grounds are outside scope.
The source is a current Indian Kanoon statutory reproduction and is not authenticated as the historical consolidation applicable at every relevant time.
No target-case judicial interpretation is supplied.

units.issue: Eviction for transfer of lease rights or subletting without written landlord consent, together with the statutory definition of tenant
units.jurisdiction: Andhra Pradesh, including the statutory Andhra-area scope quoted in the source
units.act: Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, sections 10(ii)(a) and 2(ix)
units.date_scope: The quoted section 10(ii) text refers to conduct in the Andhra area after the commencement of the Hyderabad House Rent Control Order of 1953 Fasli; no broader statute history is supplied
units.procedure_scope: A landlord seeking eviction applies to the Controller; the tenant must receive a reasonable opportunity to show cause, and the Controller must be satisfied of the statutory ground

conditions.text: A landlord seeking eviction must apply to the Controller for a direction
conditions.quote:
A landlord  who seeks  to evict  his tenant shall
          apply to  the Controller  for a  direction in that
          behalf.

conditions.text: The Controller must give the tenant a reasonable opportunity to show cause and must be satisfied of the statutory ground
conditions.quote:
If the Controller, after giving the tenant
          reasonable opportunity  of showing  cause  against
          the applicant is satisfied

conditions.text: The transfer or subletting ground requires absence of the landlord's written consent
conditions.quote:
without the written consent of
          the landlord

conditions.text: The tenant must have transferred the lease right or sublet all or part of the building, where the lease gives no right to do so
conditions.quote:
transferred  his  right  under  the  lease  or
          sublet the entire building or any portion thereof,
          if the  lease does  not confer on him any right to
          do so.

conditions.text: The statutory tenant definition excludes a person placed in occupation of a building by its tenant
conditions.quote:
does
          not include  a person  placed in  occupation of  a
          building by its tenant

limitations: The statutory language is quoted within a Supreme Court judgment and is not supplied as a complete authenticated statute history.
The material is expressly scoped to Andhra Pradesh rent law and does not establish Delhi law.
The stored text contains OCR formatting and supplies only the quoted sections.

units.issue: Application of Andhra Pradesh rent-control transfer restrictions to tenancy rights and possession transferred through a company-proposed court-sanctioned amalgamation
units.jurisdiction: Supreme Court of India applying Andhra Pradesh rent-control law
units.act: Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, including sections 10(ii)(a) and 2(ix), considered with Companies Act sections 391 and 394 and lease clause 4
units.date_scope: The supplied application concerns a tenancy beginning in January 1959 and an amalgamation sanctioned in March 1968, with dissolution stated from 16 April 1968; the source judgment is dated 17 April 1986
units.procedure_scope: Supreme Court judicial application of the supplied rent-control provisions to the amalgamation transfer; the excerpt does not independently supply the complete procedural history

conditions.text: The court treated the amalgamation as transferring the tenant company's lease and tenancy rights to the transferee company
conditions.quote:
all the  property, rights  and powers  of every  description
including all  leases and  tenancy rights  etc. of  the  1st
appellant were  transferred to  and vested  or deemed  to be
transferred and  vested in  the 2nd  appellant

conditions.text: Because the amalgamation order was based on the transferor company's own petition, the court rejected characterization of the transfer as involuntary
conditions.quote:
The order of amalgamation has
been  made  on  the  basis  of  the  petition  made  by  the
transferor company  in Company Petition No. 4 of 1968 by the
High Court of Bombay. As such it cannot be said that this is
an involuntary  transfer effected  by order  of  the  court.

conditions.text: The transfer lacked the landlord's written permission or consent required by section 10(ii)(a)
conditions.quote:
There  is   undoubtedly   no   written
permission or  consent of  the respondent  landlord to  this
transfer of  tenancy right  of the  1st appellant company

conditions.text: The court found no express statutory exception making a court-sanctioned amalgamation transfer immune from section 10(ii)(a)
conditions.quote:
There  is no  express provision in the said Act that in
case of  any involuntary transfer or transfer of the tenancy
right by  virtue of  a scheme  of amalgamation sanctioned by
the court  by its  order  under  ss.  391  and  394  of  the
Companies Act as in the present case, such transfer will not
come within  the purview of S. 10(ii)(a) of the said Act.

conditions.text: A transferee placed in possession by the tenant was not treated as a statutory tenant merely because the tenancy rights vested through the amalgamation order
conditions.quote:
the transferee company who has been put in possession of the
tenanted premises by the transferor tenant General Radio and
Appliance Co.  (P) Ltd.  cannot be deemed to be tenant under
this Act

limitations: The holding is supplied in the specific setting of a company-proposed amalgamation under sections 391 and 394 of the Companies Act and Andhra Pradesh rent law.
The excerpt also refers to lease clause 4, which prohibited subletting without written landlord permission.
The source is an exact stored judicial excerpt with OCR and page headers and does not certify a complete statute history or all possible applicability questions.
This unit does not establish Delhi rent law.

units.issue: Reported scope of Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(b) regarding sublease, assignment, other parting with possession, and involuntary sale
units.jurisdiction: Supreme Court of India reporting an earlier Supreme Court decision concerning Delhi rent law
units.date_scope: The reported precedent involved an official-liquidator sale of tenancy rights in 1961; the supplied paragraph does not independently certify the applicable historical statutory version
units.procedure_scope: Reported description of Parasaram Harnand Rao v. Shanti Prasad Narinder Kumar Jain & Anr.; the underlying matter included eviction proceedings, a warrant-of-possession recall application, second appeal, and an appeal by special leave

conditions.text: The reported holding states that section 14(b) is broad enough to cover sublease, assignment, and any other mode of parting with possession
conditions.quote:
the amplitude of S. 14(b) of the
Delhi Rent  Control Act  was wide enough not only to include
any sublease  but even  an assignment  or any  other mode by
which possession of the tenanted premises is parted.

conditions.text: The reported scope of section 14(b) does not exclude an involuntary sale
conditions.quote:
In view
of the  wide amplitude of s. 14(b), it does not exclude even
an involuntary sale.

limitations: This unit is a report of the Parasaram precedent within another Supreme Court judgment, not an independently supplied full Parasaram opinion.
The reported factual setting involved sale of tenancy rights by an official liquidator and subsequent High Court confirmation.
The supplied scope expressly does not establish a direct bank section 45 or section 9 holding.
The exact stored paragraph contains old OCR and page headers.
